result.note: Tests the type of sugar, duty status and reasons behind India's first sugar imports in nearly a decade.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, India permitted sugar imports of 1 million tonnes, its first sugar imports in nearly a decade. Consider the following statements about this decision:
items: The permitted imports are of refined sugar and attract a concessional customs duty.
Diversion of sugar to ethanol production and a weak harvest pushed domestic output below consumption.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the imports allowed are of raw sugar, and they are duty-free rather than at a concessional rate. Statement 2 is correct, since ethanol diversion and a weak harvest pushed production below domestic consumption.
questions.source: India allowed 1 million tonnes of duty-free raw sugar imports, its first sugar imports in nearly a decade, after ethanol diversion and a weak harvest pushed output below consumption.
